STRAIGHT REFERENDUM RAN ALONGSIDE the delegate election; the Secretary of State certified the statewide "For Repeal"/"Against Repeal" totals to the convention, which was required to cast its whole vote accordingly and adjourn. Brown 1938: "The vote in Arkansas July 18 was 67,622 for and 46,091 against repeal." Convention first divided 42 to 15 on the roll call, then cast a unanimous vote: "The amendment was adopted by a vote of 42 to 15, and then the unanimous vote of the convention was cast for repeal." delegates_wet=57 is that final unanimous vote (42+15). total_votes = wet+dry.

The Total vote 'Against Ratification' was Thirty-four Thousand Eight Hundred Sixteen; the whole number of names on registry lists in the State was 672,728." Identical figures in both AP tabulations. LAST STATE TO RATIFY and the only convention held in 1934, so Montana is absent from the 5 Dec 1933 AP tabulation that supplies every other state's popular vote. NO STATEWIDE POPULAR VOTE LOCATED. Delegates were chosen at the 17 Jul 1934 state primary (Plentywood Herald, 2 Aug 1934: "elected by voters of Sheridan county at the primary election as delegates in favor of repeal ... The ratification measure carried by a wide majority at the primaries"). Convention vote from Evening Star, 7 Aug 1934, p.15: "By a delegate vote of 45 to 4, Montana yesterday became the thirty-eighth State to ratify the twenty-first or repeal amendment." Corroborated by Brown 1938, which lists Montana among the six states registering any convention votes against repeal (4).

The AP tabulation of 19 Jul 1933 likewise marks Nevada "(Chosen at county conventions.)" EXCLUDE from any wet-share denominator.

NO CONVENTION WAS EVER HELD. The 7 Nov 1933 ballot both elected delegates and asked whether to call a convention; the electorate elected delegates but voted the convention down. Brown 1938: "In North Carolina the electorate voted for convention delegates, but also voted against holding a convention." The figures here are the convention-call vote as tabulated by the AP on 5 Dec 1933. Partial returns the morning after (Evening Star, 8 Nov 1933, p.4, https://www.loc.gov/resource/sn83045462/1933-11-08/ed-1/?sp=4): "Returns from 1,444 precincts of 1,831 gave 108,246 votes for repeal and 231,872 against." Included per instruction to record states that held elections without ratifying. total_votes = wet+dry.

AP tabulation, Evening Star, 5 Dec 1933, p.5 — the AP left the convention-vote column blank because the paper went to press before the Ohio convention finished. Convention vote supplied from Brown 1938: "The result of the roll call shows: Yeas, 52; Nays, none." Election date from Brown ("pursuant to your election on the seventh day of November, 1933, as a delegate to the Ohio Constitutional Convention"). total_votes = wet+dry.

STRAIGHT REFERENDUM RAN ALONGSIDE the delegate election. Brown 1938: "Oregon likewise provided that at the same election at which delegates were elected the question of ratifying or rejecting the proposed amendment should be placed before the electors in the form of a popular referendum," with candidates pledged to vote "in accordance with the will of the majority of the voters of the county from which they were candidates, as shown by the popular vote on the question." Popular figures from the AP tabulation, Evening Star, 5 Dec 1933, p.5; election date from the AP tabulation of 19 Jul 1933. The 5 dissenting convention votes are corroborated by Brown's introduction. total_votes = wet+dry.

AP tabulation, Evening Star, 5 Dec 1933, p.5 — convention-vote column blank at press time. Convention had only fifteen delegates, all elected at large; Brown 1938: "The report of the tellers is fifteen votes for the repeal of the Eighteenth Amendment and none against. The amendment is ratified and adopted by this Convention. The hour is 12:50 p.m., December 5, 1933." Election date from Brown ("election held on November 7, 1933, to constitute a convention"). total_votes = wet+dry.

AP tabulation, Evening Star, 5 Dec 1933, p.5; same figures in the AP tabulation of 19 Jul 1933. Election date left blank: Brown 1938 only says the special election was held "one week ago" relative to the 8 May convention. total_votes = wet+dry.

THE ONLY CONVENTION THAT VOTED REPEAL DOWN. Brown 1938: "The vote of the convention against repeal of the 18th amendment was unanimous, pursuant to the anti-repeal vote cast November 7 at the special election. In that election the vote stood: against repeal, 35,845; for repeal, 33,074." The dry margin was 2,771 votes — under 4 points, the closest result in the country. Convention vote of 0 to 41 from the AP tabulation, Evening Star, 5 Dec 1933, p.5, which flags the majority as against repeal. Brown's introduction: "Aside from the South Carolina convention, which was composed of delegates opposed to repeal, who voted against the ratification of the proposed amendment, the delegates favoring repeal were overwhelmingly in the majority." total_votes = wet+dry.

AP tabulation, Evening Star, 5 Dec 1933, p.5. Narrowest wet win of any ratifying state: a margin of 7,113 on 246,853 votes (50.9 percent wet). Election date from Brown 1938 ("Third Thursday of July (namely, on July 20th), 1933 ... for the purpose of electing sixty-three Delegates"). total_votes = wet+dry.

THE 36TH AND DECIDING STATE — repeal took effect on this convention's vote at 3:32 p.m. MST, 5 Dec 1933. Popular vote from the AP tabulation, Evening Star, 5 Dec 1933, p.5. Twenty-one delegates were elected, all repeal-pledged (Brown 1938: the canvassers found "the twenty-one delegates for [ratification] received a greater number of votes than the twenty-one delegates against ratification"). delegates_wet left blank: Brown's roll call records Delegate Gilmour absent and the OCR captures 19 explicit ayes of 21, so the exact aye count is not transcribable; delegates_dry=0 rests on "The vote upon the resolution is unanimous." total_votes = wet+dry.
